** New players land in Lumbridge
*** New accounts (other than Group Ironmen, who retain their route from Iron Enclave to the Iron Enclave Portal in Lumbridge, and Leagues accounts, who begin in Lumbridge courtyard) now begin their adventure at the Lumbridge lodestone, bypassing Burthorpe and Taverley paths.
**** The end of Tutorial Island and Davendale are suitably updated, unlocking and tutorialising the Lumbridge rather than Burthorpe lodestone.
**** Getting Iroh on Iron Enclave to downgrade you to standard mode now transitions to Lumbridge (rather than Burthorpe) lodestone.
** Lumbridge is now listed above Burthorpe in Death's respawn point menu.
** The Lumbridge sage has learned some lessons from his OSRS counterpart, and now has a lot more dialogue options to assist new players, such as where to find quests, what monsters to fight, where to make money, find a bank, learn about navigation, as well as lodestones, tools and the tool belt, the quest list and skill list, local history, and the wiki.
** Event noticeboards permanently mapped near Lumbridge, Varrock, Fort Forinthry, Tower of Voices lodestones, and near Draynor, Varrock, Falador, Edgeville banks have been removed.
** The talking pair of inactive villagers south of Lumbridge lodestone have been removed.
** The Iron Enclave portal north of Lumbridge lodestone is now only visible if your account can enter the portal.
** Lumbridge castle's wall has been rebuilt, once again encircling the castle, with access points from the west gatehouse and east entrance.
** A barrier has been reinstated between Lumbridge swamp and Lumbridge's town and forest.
** Poll booths at a bank in Lumbridge, Varrock, Falador, Burthorpe, Catherby, Menaphos have been removed, since active voting can be accessed from the Community interface.
** In Lumbridge courtyard, the sage's backpack is now only visible when the League's sage is visible, and the plaque's crimson pointlight is only visible when the plaque is visible. The large rock displayed to non-Leagues players instead of the plaque has been replaced with a less obtrusive set of barrels.
** Duck Quest's debris now trails from Lumbridge's swamp through the cemetery rather than between Lumbridge castle's walls.
** War supplies scenery near the west Lumbridge Castle kitchen door has been removed.
** The clue scroll "Search the crate in the left-hand tower of Lumbridge Castle" has been clarified to "Search the crate in the southern tower at the entrance to Lumbridge Castle".
** The Lumbridge worldmap text label has nudged a little to the north-west since the label's prior position rendered non-interactive the willow and rest musician icon near Lumbridge lodestone.
** The God statue east of Lumbridge has moved to north-east of Falador, in view of the crossroads overlook.
** A pair of Lumbridge guards on the bridge over the river Lum have moved to the goblin side of the bridge, as their former position might suggest the bridge was impassable.
*** Damaged floor tiles on the east side of Lum bridge have been repaired.
** Lumbridge market has been tidied up, with fewer duplicate stalls and wandering NPCs, and the NPCs that stand in place and converse are now pickpocketable.
*** Also graphically updated the remaining 5 market citizens, 2 stall merchants, and master farmer (who also now wanders only a shorter distance from the seed stall) at Lumbridge market.
*** Since Lumbridge castle's wall has been reinstated, consequently removed less accessible pickpocketable men and women immediately north of Lumbridge castle, to focus pickpocketing and stall stealing in the Lumbridge market.
*** The wooden platform has been removed from the base of the south-west and north-east (when applicable) Lumbridge market vegetable stalls, as well as the equivalent vegetable stall in Catherby market. As a side-effect this has resolved an issue where a container clipped through this platform in Catherby.
*** A white, green, magenta and cyan pointlight without source of illumination from Lumbridge market has been removed.
** The two training dummies at Lumbridge market (since it's no longer a combat academy and training dummies are available elsewhere, such as War's Retreat and Burthorpe training camp) have been removed.
*** The Blast and Hellfire hard Lumbridge task's objective has changed back from "Cast Fire Blast at a training dummy near Lumbridge market." to "Cast Fire Blast at one of the goblins or giant spiders in the Lumbridge area (including the Lumbridge catacombs and swamp)."
** The Lumbridge fishing shop has been rotated so its entrance faces Lumbridge market, like the other adjacent shops, reinforcing the market as a place of importance. Since the fishing shop has a side door, it can still be accessed from the south.
** The herald of Lumbridge has moved from near Lumbridge lodestone and bank chest to west of the market, and her pause between proclamations has tripled.
*** If you've completed the Herald the Dawn (formerly The Nexus Has You) achievement, the herald of Lumbridge now has a dialogue option to mute her overhead chat.
** The Saradominist priest and his family are no longer renting the upper level of Explorer Jack's house, south-west of Lumbridge market, and have moved on with their lives.
** The Zamorakian herbalist and their family have finally tired of the nefarious rustlings in their cellar and moved on from Lumbridge.
** Some untextured ground tiles along Lumbridge's foot paths have been corrected.
** It's been over 12 years since the Battle of Lumbridge. Nature (and the Duke of Lumbridge's fairly taxing but taxingly fair reforestation initiative) have further reclaimed the Lumbridge crater. Adventurers with long memories will likely recognise certain signature elements in the rejuvenated forest west of Lumbridge.
** Lumbridge's H.A.M. fanatics have replaced the trapdoor leading to their hideout. The trapdoor can be found at its precise location prior to the Battle of Lumbridge, in a ruin on a hill north-west of Lumbridge castle.
*** The old mine entrance east of Lumbridge has been cleared away.
** The Lumbridge farming tree patch is back at its original location, just west of Lumbridge castle. (If an amulet of nature was attuned to it, the amulet will teleport to saved coordinate until re-attuned.)
** When the 'A Christmas Reunion' quest next activates, Aoife the pixie should be on the dirt road, and described accordingly.
** By popular demand, when you have completed The World Wakes, the well in west Lumbridge forest becomes a memorial fountain, and the Saradominist preacher arrives on the scene to inform anyone who will listen that the Battle of Lumbridge happened.
** Remnants of a fence near the north road from Lumbridge to Draynor, south-west of Mill Lane Mill, have been adapted into a potato patch.
** The duck pond north-west of Lumbridge forest has moved to a position north of the restored H.A.M. ruins, resembling its original location and shape.
** A yew tree map icon has been added to the trio of yews south-east of Lumbridge's windmill.
** Entering the chicken and sheep farm adjacent to Fred the Farmer's farmhouse is now sufficient to complete the Wait, That's Not a Sheep achievement.
** Citizen dialogue in Lumbridge that referred to the 2013 Battle of Lumbridge and Lumbridge Rebuildathon as topics of recent interest has been minimised.
*** This affects the Lumbridge castle cook, Captain Harlan, Donie, Doomsayer, Duke Horacio, Explorer Jack, Father Aereck, Father Urhney, Fred the Farmer, the named and un-named Lumbridge guards, Hank, Hans, Herald of Lumbridge, Lumbridge Sage, Lactopher, Millie Miller, Man & Woman, Lumbridge general shopkeeper & assistant.
*** Issues in Donie's dialogue suggesting area quests, which referred to pre-rework versions of Rune Mysteries and What's Mine Is Yours, have been fixed. She and the Lumbridge sage also recommend additional quests, such as The Blood Pact.
*** A reference to completing Tasks for cash in Lachtopher's dialogue has been corrected.
*** A "RuneScape" when interacting with the trapdoor to Explorer Jack's cellar has been corrected to "Gielinor".

** The Digsite quest has been improved!

*** Leather boots and gloves are no longer required to dig at archaeological grids. You will still need the relevant qualification and tools.
*** Examiners will now provide the appropriate tools for each qualification, in an attempt to reduce theft on-site.
*** The Dig Site quest journal has been updated to reflect the changes made to the area.

** Herb seeds, grimy herbs, clean herbs, unfinished potions, as well as herb farming patches have been recoloured to be more consistent. It should be much easier from now to tell them apart! Thanks to everyone who has given feedback via social media.
** Generic names and examines of herb patches (such as "Herbs", "Some herbs are growing in this patch" and "Fully grown herbs") have been replaced by whatever players have planted in the respective patches (for example "Avantoe", "Avantoe is growing in this patch" and "Fully grown avantoe").
*** Note: Diseased herbs are still all using the same models, but have had their generic texts replaced, too. For example, instead of "Diseased herbs" and "These herbs have become diseased" they will now mention the herb's name, i.e. "Dwarf weed (diseased)" and "Some diseased dwarf weed. You can cure it by using a plant cure on it".
** The right-click "Guide" option should now be available at all herb patches and will consistently open the Farming skillguide with the "Herbs" filter active.
** The right-click option "Clear" is now consistently available whenever a herb is fully grown, and removes the crops instead of harvesting them.

* 
** My Arm's herb patch will now correctly tell you which seed is planted when inspected. The Scroll of Life will now also work with this patch.

** Weeded herb patches now have a configure option that players with Plant Power can use to set the default number of seeds they plant in a patch.

* 
** Inspecting a herb patch will now correctly state when its being protected by the greenfingers aura or the herb protector.

* 
** The inspect option on herb patches now tells you what type of seed was planted there.

* 
** It is now possible to use a herb protector on a herb patch whilst having a greenfingers aura active.

** If a player has blocked XP in a skill via Nastroth and lends that skill to another player via the assist system, XP earned for the assister by the assistee is now blocked.

* 
** Nastroth's skill reset now has an option to set the chosen skill to the lowest XP value, as that's the primary use case, and clarified the wording of the option to set XP to an input value.
*** Removed major skill reset options from Nastroth's dialogue, and simplified some steps in the minor reset userflow.

* 
** A player that activated Nastroth's major Defence reset should now have sufficient reputation to complete the upper Darkmeyer section of the Branches of Darkmeyer quest.

* 
** Fixed an issue where players who reset the 'Ghosts Ahoy' quest with Nastroth's Constitution and Prayer major reset now also resets Vessel of the Harbinger quest.

* 
** Players no longer require a Bank pin to clear Nastroth's reminder that a week has elapsed since they requested a skill reset.

* 
** The cancel button on Nastroth's skill selection interface for XP blocking and minor resets now goes back to Nastroth's dialogue options, instead of re-displaying the interface.
** To accommodate players who wish to lower their XP to a specific value for sentimental reasons, when choosing a minor reset, Nastroth now has a prompt to enter the specific XP value you'd like.

* 
** Nastroth's Constitution & Prayer major reset now requires Attack, Strength, Ranged, Magic, Defence and Summoning to be 10 or lower, rather than 5 or lower, to accommodate players who would need to perform a minor reset to qualify for a major reset.

* 
** The following options have been added to Nastroth in Lumbridge courtyard:
*** XP blocking: "I want to block XP from specific skills." You can choose to prevent ever getting XP in skills of your choice.
**** Note that at the request of HP pures, Constitution XP from defeating enemies in combat cannot be blocked.
*** Proof: "I want to prove I've never used an XP block/reset."
**** This toggles a tooltip on the Combat Level icon when you are inspected by a player, indicating whether XP has been blocked on your account or you have used a minor reset.
** Minor reset: To accommodate pures who have 'ruined' an account by over-levelling a skill, Nastroth can now reset your XP in a skill of your choice to its minimum, provided the chosen skill doesn't exceed level 10 (or level 15 if Constitution).
*** Unlike Nastroth's two major resets (specifically intended to reset Defence pures and Constitution & Prayer pures when Evolution of Combat released), this minor reset doesn't reset quests etc. that require the chosen skill.
** Nastroth's resets (major and minor) are now available on a six-month cooldown, instead of once per account.
*** The player must still return in 7 days to activate any reset after requesting it, and activation requires a Bank PIN.
** The limit of one major reset per account has been removed. This is to help players who are over-levelled for Nastroth's new minor reset and have already used either of Nastroth's two major resets to recover their accounts and utilise these changes.
*** To prevent exploits from major resets being used repeatedly, Nastroth will cease to provide major resets in less than six months - on Monday 18th September 2023.
*** While the limit of one major reset per account has been lifted, Nastroth's two major resets were intended for two very different types of pures, so cannot be combined.
**** If you intend to make use of one of Nastroth's major resets before they are removed... be sure to activate a major reset before activating a minor reset. Since resets share a six-month cooldown and major resets will be removed in less than six months, if Nastroth is waiting six months after a minor reset, you won't be able to use a major reset before they are removed. Nastroth requires you to wait 7 days after requesting a reset to come back and activate it. So if you have requested a minor reset and prefer to use a major reset, there's time to change your mind if you haven't yet returned in a week to activate the minor reset.
**** Also note that Nastroth's major resets were intended to specifically reset two types of pures at the dawn of the Evolution of Combat and have not been maintained, so until their removal, you use major resets at your own risk.
** Keepsake Box checks now occur before Nastroth skill reset warnings, so that if a skill reset fails due to having keepsaked items, the reset does not prematurely go on 7 day cooldown.

** If the player currently has a basic challenge to do, Challenge Mistresses and Nastroth in Lumbridge now give a chat option to skip any of these challenges. This is so that a new player who does not want to engage in certain skills and/or get the XP from them does not have to complete all the basic challenge objectives.

** Significantly reworked Daemonheim:

** With the recent updates to Construction via Fort Forinthry, protean planks have been redesigned to be more in line with other protean resources.
** Protean planks can no longer be used to build things, and you cannot cut protean logs into planks (you can still convert them, but through the usual 3:2 conversion of any protean to any other).
** They now behave more like protean bars, where players have level banded Make-X interactions which consume one plank at a time, at a rate of one every 7 ticks (this can be reduced to 6 with the protean powerup). These produce no output other than XP.
*** To start the Make-X interaction, the player will need to interact with either a construction hotspot in their player-owned house, a workbench in a POH or a portable workbench.
*** These changes represent a decrease in XP per hour from the items, but also represent a decrease in skilling intensity, in keeping with other proteans.
**** It is however a buff to XP per protean plank at level 60 and above, topping out at level 90 with x2.25 more XP per plank than before.

** Ring of Death's cooldown is no longer removed during certain boss phase changes.
** The Ring of Death's effect now correctly applies to all Instakill mechanics.
** Dev note! Thanks for feedback on the Ring of Death since the recent update. You've told us that damage mitigation effects combined with healing abilities make the Ring of Death's effect too easy to survive, which trivialises many instakill mechanics.. Instakills were also confusing, as we had multiple forms with the same visual effects. These are now defined as:
*** Full instakill: No signs or Ring of Death allowed - will display the skull with 'Instant Kill' text.
*** Soft instakill: Signs and Ring of Death allowed - will display the skull without text.
*** High damage: Deals lots of damage but isn't technically an instakill.
*** The starting damage value will now be 20% of the killing blow, within the range of 150 to 2000. A soft instakill will automatically start at 2,000, so you can survive the mechanic, but it will still be tough to survive long enough for the kill. The timer will now last until you either die or return to a safe area, allowing higher-level players to survive longer... but not indefinitely.
*** Following these changes, the sign will now take priority over the Ring of Death and be the first to activate.

** Fletching buffs for saving resources and auto-stringing unstrung bows now have additive percentage chance when multiple buffs with the same effect are active, instead of rolling for each buff separately and choosing the first one to proc (e.g. Crystal Knife and Wergali incense). This more accurately represents the desired outcome of stacking random chance buffs and provides an increased probability for the effect to proc.
** Fixed an issue where the portable fletcher would award the additional XP and consume the resources for stringing two bows at once, but not give an extra strung bow.
** Buffs for saving fletching resources no longer send the extra resources to the bank, instead they are not removed from the inventory. The fletched product will be sent to the bank if saving resources resulted in not having enough space to receive it.
** Saving logs via a buff while fletching an unstrung bow or crossbow stock would previously not subtract an action from the MakeX queue, allowing extras to be fletched within the same queue. Although this can be a useful feature, it has been removed to remain consistent with the other instances where the buff to save fletching resources procs, and to prevent the seemingly-buggy behaviour of the MakeX interface which would not increment a craft in the progress bar and add more time onto the countdown clock. It was also a consideration that a player may not wish to use their saved logs on crafting another of the same item.
** The portable fletcher no longer provides a chance to string two crossbows at once.
** The portable fletcher now allows a chance to save resources when making unstrung crossbows, as well as producing two at once. If both effects proc, saving resources will only apply to one of the fletched items.

** Spirit gems converted from pouch-holding to charm-saving.
** Following player feedback, we have now reverted the changes made earlier this month to the Summoning skill. Any players who still have uncharged pouches can now convert them into the relevant amount of experience and pouches.
** Following on from this, spirit gems have undergone the following changes:
*** Players with charges left in their gem can now use up the charges for the correct amount of experience. As players will not receive pouches for this, their gem will convert into a new-style spirit gem.
*** Each charge in a new-style spirit gem now equates to a free charm when crafting pouches. There is a varying trigger chance for the gems: from 10% for a sapphire, to 60% for an onyx.
*** Spirit gems can now be equipped in the pocket slot.

** You can now visit another player's uncharted isle and toggle restrictions on who can visit your Island.

* 
** Players can now change their Skybox/Filters in Dungeoneering, the Uncharted Isles and the Player-Owned House.

* 
** Treasure chests on Uncharted Isles now consistently use the correct open model for their type.
** Filtered messages have been added for Uncharted Isles' rare resources at different stages of depletion.

* 
** You can now travel to the Uncharted Isles from the quartermaster in Port Sarim, if you have previously visited at least one Uncharted Isle.

* 
** The Arc travel map interface now opens to the Uncharted Isles page if last selected, saving players who wish to travel to another island one click.
** The blocking on certain uncharted isles has been fixed.
** Mushroom clusters now look better when spawning on a hill on an uncharted island.

* 
** The click radius of chimes and sea shells found on uncharted isles has been increased, making them easier to interact with.
** Tortles on uncharted isles now have a reduced wander range, preventing overlapping and collision issues.

* 
** Uncharted isle NPCs now drop chimes in increased amounts as well as some flavour items.
** Players are now able to find supply crates on uncharted isles.
** Low-tier resources will now stay on claimed islands, even when logging out.
** Long voyages now cost 20 supplies (down from 25).
** Median Expeditions can now have 2 to 3 rare resources (up from 1 to 2).
** Long Voyages can now have 3 to 5 rare resources (up from 2 to 3).
** Players who had islands claimed prior the update can now find new resources on their island.
** An issue where an island would have less rare resources than intended has been fixed.
** Players will no longer find wushrooms washed ashore on uncharted isles. Sea shells can now be found instead.

* 
** Prawn balls can now be received whilst fishing within The Arc and Uncharted Isles.

* 
** You will now find even more items washed up on uncharted islands, based on the island's size. Logging out will still wash unpicked items away.
** You will now be able to find some different items washed up on uncharted islands, such as fruit or bones.
** You can now use surge on uncharted islands.
** The messages you receive when claiming an island to clarify that claiming another will NOT refresh the daily cap on claimed islands have been refined.
** Claiming a new uncharted island will now allow you to exhaust it correctly, even if their previously claimed island had been exhausted.

* 
** The player's own ship (not rowboat) in the Uncharted Isles now has shadows and reflections.
** Smoothed out some underwater issues on uncharted islands where raised bumps were appearing.
** Hermit crabs no longer visit the waters surrounding the Uncharted Isles.
** Chimes are now occasionally dropped by NPCs found on uncharted islands.
** The issue where in rare cases high-level resources on uncharted islands were depleting after just one harvest, has now been fixed.

** Players with two or four scraps of scripture will receive additional scraps next time they open a phylactery, rounding their total scraps to a figure that's divisible by 5.
*** The phylactery was modified to allow players who had obtained an uneven amount of scripture to gain an amount that would balance out the number of scriptures they had, if the total amount of scraps they obtained ended in 2, 4, 6, or 8. This was due to some players obtaining multiple sets of 2 scraps prior to the 17 July update.

* 
** The phylactery drop rate from the Magister has been made slightly lower, but the individual scripture drop rates have been adjusted to give a minimum of 5 and a larger average.
*** Prior to this update, players could obtain either 2, 5, 10 or 25 scraps when breaking phylacteries. The chance of 2 scraps was removed following player feedback, and substituted with 15 scraps, although the drop rate of the phylactery was made slightly rarer to balance it out.

** As you might have heard, there’s been a few changes down on the farm. Last week, we addressed some of your biggest concerns about the update to Player Owned Farms and laid out how we planned to fix them. Today’s update sees these changes out in the wild. You can look forward to an improved XP-to-effort ratio, a deeper farming experience, and more player-to-player interactions than you can shake a rake at. Why not head on down to Ardougne and check out the new and improved farm for yourself?
** Harvest XP has been reduced by 50%.
** Animal XP is now based on their health and happiness.
*** This is to encourage players to engage with their farm more actively. Now the happiness and health of the animals adjusts the XP to a percentage of their average, to a minimum of 10% of their maximum value. This means that you need to keep your animals fed and healthy if you want to maintain their best XP rates.
** Harvest XP can now be boosted by items and bonus XP
*** You can now use any XP boosting reward or device while harvesting. While this doesn’t include double XP weekends, it means that those who are going for efficiency can see an increase in the base XP to somewhere near the pre-nerf values.
** Reduced breeding outside of breeding pens.
*** Animals in the small pen will take 1.5x as long to breed as animals in the breeding pen
*** Animals in the medium pen will take 2x as long to breed as animals in the breeding pen
*** Animals in the large pen will take 3x as long to breed as animals in the breeding pen
** Reduced the amount of animals the collector farmhand can hold.
*** Currently the collector can hold 90 animals, which is excessive. The current format means that there’s little reason to trade as players will just collect a ton of animals over the course of a few weeks. So the plan is to reduce the collector’s capacity to 10 of each breed, for a total of 30 possible animals. Note: This won’t remove any animals she is currently holding over that limit, merely prevent more animals from being stored. The collector is still a great investment, but now we encourage people to sell more animals to get the best results (for both the buyer and the seller).
** The rate at which animals feed has been increased.
*** To keep things simple, we’ve decided to make it so that each animal eats 1 food every hour. Put simply, this means that an animal's health and happiness will now improve at twice the rate, while still allowing players to leave their farms alone for a few days and check back in to top things up.
*** Additionally, we’ve increased the amount of food which can be added via left click. Now you can fill the entire trough in one go.
** Increased the benefits of shiny enhancing traits.
*** These traits have been doubled in effectiveness, meaning you are much more likely to get a shiny animal if you breed these traits. However, we recognise that breeding traits isn’t an exact science so we’ve made an additional change.
** Increased the hereditary nature of traits
*** All traits now have a much higher base chance of being passed on to their children. It’s not 100%, but you should see it being much easier to breed the traits you want into your animals, whether it be the shiny boosting traits or traits like jovial and immune.
** Increased the value of shiny animals
*** To give even more value to shiny animals, they will now produce 25% more XP than their base animal (up from 10%). This means that if you aim to breed shiny animals, you should see a higher rate of XP as a reward for the effort you have put into the farm.

** Various changes made to address complaints listed in the Player Owned Farm - Changes Blog.
** Animal XP is now based on their health and happiness.
*** This is to encourage players to engage with their farm more actively. Now the happiness and health of the animals adjusts the XP to a percentage of their average, to a minimum of 10% of their maximum value. This means that you need to keep your animals fed and healthy if you want to maintain their best XP rates.
** The rate at which animals feed has been increased.
*** To keep things simple, we’ve decided to make it so that each animal eats 1 food every hour. Put simply, this means that an animal's health and happiness will now improve at twice the rate, while still allowing players to leave their farms alone for a few days and check back in to top things up.
*** Additionally, we’ve increased the amount of food which can be added via left click. Now you can fill the entire trough in one go.

** Added to game.
*** Passage of the Abyss is a pocket-slot item that can hold up to six different compacted jewellery all in one item! No need to carry around all of those teleports - now you can do it in a single item.
*** Passage of the abyss can be created on a workbench after discovering the blueprint with 118 Invention. The player requires: 1 alchemical onyx, 50 magic components, and 1 teleportation compactor.
*** It can store up to six of any of the compacted jewellery made from Invention.
**** To add a particular piece of jewellery to the Passage of the Abyss requires 100x the maximum charge of the jewellery. So to add an Amulet of Glory, you would need 400 charges.
**** You can combine any of the different forms of an item to reach this number, including an already compacted version of the item.
*** Passage of the Abyss can be recoloured so that you can have multiple and have different teleports on each item.
*** Teleporting with Passage of the Abyss removes charges from the item and can be recharged at a rate of 500 charges per fortunate component.

** Ring of Death's cooldown is no longer removed during certain boss phase changes.
** The Ring of Death's effect now correctly applies to all Instakill mechanics.
** Dev note! Thanks for feedback on the Ring of Death since the recent update. You've told us that damage mitigation effects combined with healing abilities make the Ring of Death's effect too easy to survive, which trivialises many instakill mechanics.. Instakills were also confusing, as we had multiple forms with the same visual effects. These are now defined as:
*** Full instakill: No signs or Ring of Death allowed - will display the skull with 'Instant Kill' text.
*** Soft instakill: Signs and Ring of Death allowed - will display the skull without text.
*** High damage: Deals lots of damage but isn't technically an instakill.
*** The starting damage value will now be 20% of the killing blow, within the range of 150 to 2000. A soft instakill will automatically start at 2,000, so you can survive the mechanic, but it will still be tough to survive long enough for the kill. The timer will now last until you either die or return to a safe area, allowing higher-level players to survive longer... but not indefinitely.
*** Following these changes, the sign will now take priority over the Ring of Death and be the first to activate.

** Ring of Death's cooldown is no longer removed during certain boss phase changes.
** The Ring of Death's effect now correctly applies to all Instakill mechanics.
** Dev note! Thanks for feedback on the Ring of Death since the recent update. You've told us that damage mitigation effects combined with healing abilities make the Ring of Death's effect too easy to survive, which trivialises many instakill mechanics.. Instakills were also confusing, as we had multiple forms with the same visual effects. These are now defined as:
*** Full instakill: No signs or Ring of Death allowed - will display the skull with 'Instant Kill' text.
*** Soft instakill: Signs and Ring of Death allowed - will display the skull without text.
*** High damage: Deals lots of damage but isn't technically an instakill.
*** The starting damage value will now be 20% of the killing blow, within the range of 150 to 2000. A soft instakill will automatically start at 2,000, so you can survive the mechanic, but it will still be tough to survive long enough for the kill. The timer will now last until you either die or return to a safe area, allowing higher-level players to survive longer... but not indefinitely.
*** Following these changes, the sign will now take priority over the Ring of Death and be the first to activate.

* 
** A Phoenix necklace will no longer reset the cooldown and effect of the Ring of Death.
** The Ring of Death's 'Return to Life' passive no longer prevents player from looting boss corpses and chests after the fight.

* 
** God Books, Illuminated God Books, and Erethdor's Grimoire now toggle 'off' upon death while you have a Ring of Death equipped. This behaviour is in-line with scrimshaws and intended to prevent charges from being wasted while preparing for combat.

* 
** Item effects are no longer cleared from the buff bar when the Ring of Death activates.

* 
** Overcharged rings of death can now be worn via the action bar.

** Herb seeds, grimy herbs, clean herbs, unfinished potions, as well as herb farming patches have been recoloured to be more consistent. It should be much easier from now to tell them apart! Thanks to everyone who has given feedback via social media.
** Generic names and examines of herb patches (such as "Herbs", "Some herbs are growing in this patch" and "Fully grown herbs") have been replaced by whatever players have planted in the respective patches (for example "Avantoe", "Avantoe is growing in this patch" and "Fully grown avantoe").
*** Note: Diseased herbs are still all using the same models, but have had their generic texts replaced, too. For example, instead of "Diseased herbs" and "These herbs have become diseased" they will now mention the herb's name, i.e. "Dwarf weed (diseased)" and "Some diseased dwarf weed. You can cure it by using a plant cure on it".
** The right-click "Guide" option should now be available at all herb patches and will consistently open the Farming skillguide with the "Herbs" filter active.
** The right-click option "Clear" is now consistently available whenever a herb is fully grown, and removes the crops instead of harvesting them.

* 
** Diseased Farming patches will no longer die!

* 
** Diseased herbs has now 'Cure' as the first option.

* 
** Inspecting a herb patch will now correctly state when its being protected by the greenfingers aura or the herb protector.

* 
** The inspect option on herb patches now tells you what type of seed was planted there.

* 
** It is now possible to use a herb protector on a herb patch whilst having a greenfingers aura active.

* 
** Temporary increased yield for allotment and herb patches added until 7 January 2019.

* 
** The Farming skillcape perk message now correctly reflects the master farmer outfit's ability to clean herbs.
** Signs of the porter will now work in conjunction with collecting clean herb from patches (via the Farming outfits) as well as collecting the Player Owned Farm honey varieties from the Apiaries.

* 
** Farmer's Catalyst fragment and Combined Catalyst fragment added as a reward for the new quest, Sliske's Endgame. These allow the harvesting of shadow herbs from dead herb patches, which can be cleaned for Herblore XP.

*** This week the Rex Matriarchs come roaring into the game with a new combat challenge for experienced fighters. 
*** You'll go up against three respawning bosses. Each has a different strength to test your mettle, but also a different weakness to be exploited. Note that access to Anachronia is required to take on this challenge. So what are you waiting for? Grab your best gear and head to central Anachronia. The lair of the Rex Matriarchs awaits...

Following the events of Azzanadra's Quest old friends have become terrible foes, and certain factions have decided it's time to knock some sense into each other. Their stage is the Archaeology Guild, their audience, the looming shadow of the Monolith.

** Ek-ZekKil has been reworked with a brand-new special attack and passive effect, themed around Zuk's iconic duels. It now boosts your melee abilities and shines in longer fights.
*** Removed the current special attack, Igneous Cleave, and replaced it with a new one: Igneous Showdown. This new ability has a 1-minute cooldown, and costs 65% Adrenaline. Activating Igneous Showdown will initially deal moderate damage to your target and mark them as your Flamebound Rival until either they are defeated or you fall in combat. This mark can be transferred to another enemy by using the special attack on a new target; however, you can only have one rival active at a time. **** +5% melee damage against your Flamebound Rival
**** 5% reduced damage taken from them
**** Using Igneous Showdown on the same rival deals additional damage. 
*** The Ek-ZekKil now features a passive effect called Ashen Vow, which is active while the weapon is equipped. This passive empowers three of your melee abilities:
**** Pulverise: Adrenaline cost reduced from 100% → 60%
**** Quake: Increases the Base Hit Chance debuff on all affected enemies from 2 → 4
**** Lesser Smash: Increases damage from 95–115% → 150–170%
**** Smash: Increases damage from 100–120% → 160–180%
**Any Ek-ZekKils placed in an essence of finality amulet are removed and refunded to account for the new change.

***** For every stack of Abyssal Parasite, the target will take damage every three cycles, for 15 cycles in total.

***** The Abyssal Parasite shares similarities with Corruption Shot, except it will also tag and aggro its targets when it jumps to them. Gruesome!

** Boss Enrage Unlocking has now been unlocked.
*** Players can now start at any enrage level they choose, up to 4,000%.
*** To respect the time and achievements of our most dedicated Zamorak players, the Zamorak encounter will initially allow entry up to 4,000% enrage only. Once 4,000% has been defeated, players will still be able to push beyond this threshold.
*** The only change being, a successful Zamorak kill at your highest enrage above 4,000% will now increase enrage in 100% increments (up from 10%).

*** The Seed Pack formerly contained 3 sweetcorn, 6 tomato, and 2 limpwurt seeds. It could rarely include magic and yew seeds. It now contains one batch of the following seeds: 16 ranarr, 16 limpwurt, 16 cadantine, 16 toadflax, 16 snapdragon, 12 avantoe, 12 watermelon, 1 lantadyme or 1 dwarf weed seed.
** Those of you who've completed The Void Stares Back can buy Jessika's sword – an off-hand companion to Korasi's sword – for commendations.
** The rewards interface has been clearly organised into four tabs, so all this is easier to find. There's also an additional rewards vendor by the outpost's docks.

** A new ritual has manifested in Um to help players gather up Ectoplasm. It's called 'Manifest Ectoplasm', and will require level 95 Necromancy. When completed it will reward 55 Ectoplasm as baseline, perfect for restocking on supplies!

* 
** Increased the drop rate of moonstones from ritual disturbances.

* 
** Using the Captain's Log with a fixed camera on the ritual site will no longer break the fixed camera.

* 
** Fixed an issue where occasionally Glyphs may not be recognised for the active ritual.

* 
** Ritual components can no longer revert to a locked state.
** Ritual components no longer randomly lose their durability border colours during rituals.
** Pathing has been improved for sparkling Glyph and Soul Storm random events.
** The Ritual Progression bar no longer shows progression as divided by 10 in Legacy Combat Mode.

* 
** We will be adjusting Ritual XP rates in the following ways:
*** Ritual Output XP is increased.
*** Random events will have their XP rewards reduced.
*** At levels 60+, XP will be reduced overall by approximately 20%, with Rituals below level 60 affected less than this.

* 
** The ritual minigame tab now shows the output as affected by any multipliers, such as Multiply Glyphs and the Underworld Grimoire.

* 
** Made several improvements to ritual random events:
*** Added smoke clouds when spawning Wandering Soul and Corrupt Glyphs.
*** Added passive audio to Soul Storm and Defile.
*** Added spawn audio to Shambling Horror and Corrupt Glyphs.
*** Added success audio to Shambling Horror, Corrupt Glyphs and Soul Storm.
*** Added audio when the Defile Pool crackles.
*** Increased the brightness of the Wandering Soul and Shambling Horror.
*** Slowed down the speed of the Wandering Soul.
*** Changed the pop-up text when clicking on the Shambling Horror to chatbox only.
*** Tweaked the Shambling Horror so you can continue to guess on ritual components after failing, without having to reclick the Horror.
*** Moved pop-up text from when random events spawn and despawn to appear over the random event, rather than in the middle of the screen.
*** Improved 'funkiness' of forcewalk when completing random events.
** Depositing All into the focus storage will no longer give an error message.
** Clicking away from the ritual platform before starting no longer force-walks players back to the platform.
** The Dragonkin Bones model on the ritual pedestal no longer uses the Rune Dragon Bones model.
** Teleporting to the ritual site via the Underworld Grimoire, with fixed camera view on, will now show the ritual site correctly.
** Wandering Souls can be dismissed during Rituals when op'd without the need to re-op.
** Added messaging that says how much of the focus object is left in the focus storage when used.
** The materials required to repair a ritual component are now listed in the error message.
** Added messaging when attempting to Repair All on a component you don't meet the level requirements to repair.
** The front two ritual light source spots have been moved, to clear a path between the ritual platform and the pedestal. Note that some of your light sources may now be in different places.
** Unavailable focus objects in the ritual selection interface now use a grey colouring, for higher contrast against the available focus objects.
** The fixed camera angle for the ritual site has been adjusted to give a better view of the components behind the pedestal.

* 
** When hovering over the input items in the ritual selection interface, a tooltip will now display the amount you have in your focus storage, and in your backpack.
** If you have none of the same focus object left, the highest tier focus object will now be placed on the pedestal after finishing a ritual, rather than the lowest.
** A new Necromancy gameplay settings option has been added, which will allow ritual output to be sent to the focus storage, rather than the ritual chest.
** A message is now output in the chatbox when a focus object is used from the focus storage.
** A message is now output in the chatbox when a focus object is removed from the pedestal.
** A message is now output in the chatbox when a ritual is completed, detailing the rewards.
** The spacebar will now consistently work to select a ritual in the ritual selection interface.
** A message will now appear in the player's chatbox when a ritual disturbance spawns.

* 
** Fixed an issue where some players were blocked from progressing the ritual tutorial by mounds of dust. Affected players are now able to clear the mounds and continue their rituals.
** Defile event & Necromancer's Tomes of Experience are re-enabled. Tomes now go directly to inventory or on the floor.
** Tweaked XP gained from Ritual random events. 
** Capped the types of random events that can spawn for T1, T2 and T3 rituals. 

* 
** The Defile ritual disturbance has been temporarily disabled—including the tomes that come from them—due to some unexpected behaviour.
** Players can no longer place portable skilling stations, challenge gems or light fires on the ritual site.

** Adjusted the rates of rare items in Sanctum of Rebirth, with the new ecliptic components adding a sink to Sanctum's weapons.
*** Weapons drop table:
**** Normal Mode: 1/50 → 1/75
**** Hard Mode: 1/40 → 1/60
*** Prayer & Scripture drop table:
**** Normal Mode: 1/90 → 1/125
**** Hard Mode: 1/80 → 1/100
*** Shard of Genesis Essence: 1/80 → 1/75
** A few commons have become a bit too plentiful, so they're being swapped out for more used commons to allow the prices to recover.
*** Molten glass → Extreme necromancy 1 dose (3-6)
*** Water orb → Fellstalk seed (1-3)

* 
** Added in a number of new VO voicelines for Nakatra within the Sanctum of Rebirth, to assist with knowing which attack is coming and when.
** Added in a number of new VO voicelines for Nakatra within the Sanctum of Rebirth at each phase transition and boss death, to add flavour and audio queues.

* 
** Fixed an issue where the extra health UI was not removed on leaving the Shadowsands in the Sanctum of Rebirth.

* 
** From now on free-to-play players won't be able to travel to the Sanctum of Rebirth by taking the gondola. Players that logged out within the Sanctum of Rebirth on a free-to-play world can take the gondola back to the City of Um.

* 
** Fixed an issue where bars above the Sanctum of Rebirth bosses overlapped during the fight.
** Fixed an issue where using defensive abilities, such as Resonance, would incorrectly display a miss/shield hitmarker instead of 1 damage.
** Fixed an issue where the shadowsands gorilla akhs within the Sanctum of Rebirth would move unintentionally. Creepy!
** Added UI popups to the Sanctum of Rebirth in order to give players information about the death mechanic within Normal Mode:
*** Implemented a UI popup for 'Divine Protection' for when the buff is applied. This will appear the first time a player begins an encounter.
*** Implemented a UI popup for 'Resurrection Sickness' for when the debuff is applied. This will appear the first time a player begins an encounter.
*** Implemented a one-off message that will appear the first time the player interacts with the Sanctum entrance, noting that deaths are safe in Normal Mode.
** Fixed an issue where the moonstone shards within the Sanctum of Rebirth would retaliate when attacked.
** Improved the clean up time for moonstone shards within the Sanctum of Rebirth to allow for much smoother movement when traversing the environments.

* 
** Accuracy Fix: Corrected accuracy miscalculation and adjusted defence values for Sanctum of Rebirth bosses to maintain hit chance balance.
** VFX Tweaks: Implemented temporary visual effects tweaks in the Sanctum of Rebirth to improve performance for all players.
** Vermyx: Reflected souls are counted correctly now when they spawned on the same tile.
** Fixed an issue that caused the rare drop spotanim in the Sanctum of Rebirth to disappear if a player used Surge at the same time as the spotanim triggers.
** Nakatra's Shockwave attack also deals damage in the centre now.
** Fixed an issue where the broadcast message showed a higher kill number when a player got the Sanctum of Rebirth boss pet.
** Fixed an issue that made it possible to open the treasure chest outside of the Sanctum of Rebirth without entering the bank pin.
** Following feedback, the hitbox for Nefthys within the Sanctum of Rebirth has been increased slightly to make it easier to attack.
** Extended Safe Death: Enjoy safe death mechanics until 4th August.
*** The Calendar entries for Sanctum of Rebirth and Free Death week are also extended until the 4th August.

** The Paradox spell has been turned into a self buff, extended in length and made usable with a lot more skilling nodes.
*** Increased the duration of Paradox to 1 minute and rebalanced the runes needed.
*** Added the arc, magnetic minnow and swarm fishing, barbarian fishing, Croesus front fishing (not the boss!), rocktail, cavefish and ghostly sole to the list of fish that work with Paradox.
*** Stopped the dwarven fish extractor from allowing players to fish bait-free while crystallise or Paradox are active.
*** Stopped the dwarven fish extractor animation from playing while crystallise or Paradox are active.
*** Paradox now works for all major hunter methods except big game hunter and whirligigs, including the Croesus front outside the boss arena.
*** Mining with Paradox now gives +1 ore and +25% mining damage to account for both low and high level methods - previously, the low level methods were not impacted by the +100% mining damage at all, and without the extra mining damage, higher level methods don't benefit by just having Paradox on until you eventually get an ore.
*** Paradox now works on rune essence, silver, gold, concentrated gold, clay and soft clay, granite, limestone, regular sandstone, gem rocks, crablets and the Croesus front mining outside the boss arena.
*** The Dwarven Ramhammer animation now doesn't show if the player is using crystallise or Paradox to signify that it doesn't provide any benefits.
*** Added Croesus front woodcutting (outside boss arena) and bamboo to the list of resources Paradox works on.
*** Stopped the dwarven chainaxe animation from working while Paradox or Crystallise are active.

*** This is visible on the player's debuff bar on the icon.
*** Obelisks are now more dangerous.
**** Damage output is doubled from 2k
**** They damage at a range of 40, up from 18
**** They heal twice as much as before
**** They damage players every 4 cycles, up from 5
*** Players must charge at least 2 fragments before clicking to reform Tumeken.
*** A gorilla ahk will now spawn and fixate on a random player when a fragment is charged past 50%.
**** These gorillas have 250k HP and share the gatekeeper gorilla behaviour (Can stun, will charge at the player)
**** These have a 30 second cooldown from when they spawn, meaning as long as you do not lose progress past 50% on a fragment you will only get 1 gorilla per fragment

*** Platform minions HP increased to 75k.
*** Shadow clone max HP increased to 350k.
*** Increased damage of shadow clones when in close proximity of other clones.
**** 25% defensive penetration added to clones.
**** Additional 10% per proximity stack.
** P7:
*** When voking towards an altar, the player now must take the direct hit and can no longer surge/dive out of the way.
*** When taking the hit the player will receive interceptor debuff, the same as P5 (Max player count -1).
*** This means a different player will need to voke the next altar until they run out of interceptor stacks.
*** Het healing increased from 25% -> 100%.

** Herb seeds, grimy herbs, clean herbs, unfinished potions, as well as herb farming patches have been recoloured to be more consistent. It should be much easier from now to tell them apart! Thanks to everyone who has given feedback via social media.
** Generic names and examines of herb patches (such as "Herbs", "Some herbs are growing in this patch" and "Fully grown herbs") have been replaced by whatever players have planted in the respective patches (for example "Avantoe", "Avantoe is growing in this patch" and "Fully grown avantoe").
*** Note: Diseased herbs are still all using the same models, but have had their generic texts replaced, too. For example, instead of "Diseased herbs" and "These herbs have become diseased" they will now mention the herb's name, i.e. "Dwarf weed (diseased)" and "Some diseased dwarf weed. You can cure it by using a plant cure on it".
** The right-click "Guide" option should now be available at all herb patches and will consistently open the Farming skillguide with the "Herbs" filter active.
** The right-click option "Clear" is now consistently available whenever a herb is fully grown, and removes the crops instead of harvesting them.

** It's been over 12 years since the Battle of Lumbridge. Nature (and the Duke of Lumbridge's fairly taxing but taxingly fair reforestation initiative) have further reclaimed the Lumbridge crater. Adventurers with long memories will likely recognise certain signature elements in the rejuvenated forest west of Lumbridge.
*** Immediately north of the dirt road cutting through west Lumbridge forest is a ruined building on a hill, infested by spiders. There are also goblins.
*** A pack of giant rats loiter in the south-east corner of west Lumbridge forest.
*** Rabbits are still a thing, albeit (on account of the giant rats) fewer in number, including one called Squiggles.
*** Squiggles in west Lumbridge forest are now attackable like other rabbits, as nature intended.
*** A unicorn features in the south-west corner of the forest for no immediately apparent reason.
*** A notoriously aggressive mugger lurks in the south of the forest. He's properly annoying.
*** There are a few yew trees in west Lumbridge forest (just for yew).
** Lumbridge's H.A.M. fanatics have replaced the trapdoor leading to their hideout. The trapdoor can be found at its precise location prior to the Battle of Lumbridge, in a ruin on a hill north-west of Lumbridge castle.
*** The old mine entrance east of Lumbridge has been cleared away.
*** Dialogue and quest journal in the One Small Favour once again describes the H.A.M. hideout as infested with spiders and goblins.
*** An animation issue when picking the lock of the H.A.M. The hideout entrance has been fixed.
*** Removed some wood slats from the upper level of the H.A.M. ruin for ease of clicking its trapdoor.
** The Lumbridge farming tree patch is back at its original location, just west of Lumbridge castle. (If an amulet of nature was attuned to it, the amulet will teleport to saved coordinate until re-attuned.)
** When the 'A Christmas Reunion' quest next activates, Aoife the pixie should be on the dirt road, and described accordingly.
** Since the forest west of Lumbridge once again bears little resemblance to a crater, various accessible text referring to it as the Lumbridge crater (that isn't linked to a specific period in the storyline when it was a crater) has been updated to reference a forest west of Lumbridge.
** By popular demand, when you have completed The World Wakes, the well in west Lumbridge forest becomes a memorial fountain, and the Saradominist preacher arrives on the scene to inform anyone who will listen that the Battle of Lumbridge happened.
** A line of the Saradominist preacher's dialogue referring to west Lumbridge forest as a crater in the present tense has been corrected.

** For this update, we're bringing out Mod Stu's gamejam project which allows Free to Play to get a taste of the construction skill! Here's the full list of changes:
*** Alfred Stonemason near Taverley lodestone now has options to buy, move and redecorate a player-owned house on F2P worlds.
*** Alfred Stonemason in Taverley now sells modest quantities of bronze nails, bolts of cloth, a watering can, and low-level garden plants to aid new players in starting to furnish their player-owned house.
*** The Construction achievement path has been expanded to introduce making planks, removing furniture, and building a wider variety of furniture. Its Membership requirement has been removed.
*** The estate agent is now visible to F2P, also allowing access to options to buy, move (F2P areas only) and redecorate a player-owned house on F2P worlds.
*** F2P can now buy a player-owned house for the usual 1,000 coins.
*** F2P can now enter their player-owned house.
*** PoH is now accessible on F2P worlds. Some members-only room features may still be restricted.
*** The garden supplier in Falador is now visible to F2P and they can buy bagged dead tree and bagged plant 1.
*** The Construction Guide book from the estate agent is now a F2P object, and has been updated to account for F2P Construction changes.
*** Sawdust is once again a F2P object. It's still useless.
*** The sawmill operator's shop (including the operator in Taverley) is now available to F2P.
*** The bolt of cloth is now a F2P object.
*** Bagged dead tree and bagged plant 1 are now F2P objects.
*** F2P can now build a garden (1,000 coins) and the following hotspots: Exit portal, Decorative rock, Dead tree, Plant, Fern.
*** F2P can now build a parlour (1,000 coins) and the following hotspots: Crude wooden chair, Brown rug, Clay fireplace, Torn curtains, Wooden bookcase.
*** F2P can now build a kitchen (5,000 coins) and the following hotspots up to level 5 Construction: Firepit, Cat blanket.
*** F2P can now read F2P books in a PoH bookcase for which they have met the requirements.
*** F2P can now sit on chairs and light the fireplace in their parlour.
*** F2P can now cook on the firepit in their kitchen.
*** F2P can now use their cat or kitten on the cat blanket in their kitchen to make them rest.
*** The following are now F2P in the Construction skillguide: Basic wood house style (2,500 coins), Daytime house lighting (5,000 coins), Rough grass grounds style (5,000 coins), Garden (Room), Parlour (Room), Kitchen (Room), Clay fireplace, Firepit, Crude wooden chair, Torn curtains, Wooden bookcase, Low-level plants, Decorative rock, Dead tree, Cat blanket.
*** The following challenges are now available to F2P: crude wooden chairs, wooden bookcases.
*** The menus for moving and re-decorating a house have been rewritten.
*** Fixed an issue where the option to build plants in the PoH was illuminated when the player didn't meet the Construction requirement.
*** The following features of PoH are now disabled on F2P worlds to accommodate lapsed F2P and house visits: spawning and storing of member pets in menagerie, pet feeder, withdrawing member equipment in costume room, study lectern, offering and burning incense at chapel altar, aquarium and dungeon access, scrying pool and portals to P2P areas, boxing ring, (clockwork) workbench.
